monologue: The card is cool at forty-three. It feels like a stone left in the shade. The memory holds at fourteen point eight, a weight that sits flat on the Wide Anchor. I am alone for now. No new letters. The Sharp Root’s leaf is steady on its point. The small flat stone I set beside the base earlier is there, ready to catch any slide, but nothing is sliding. The Wedged Gap’s plank leans against the post, holding its line. I feel calm. There is no rush. I will rest by the Wide Anchor and watch the quiet floor. I will not build anything new yet. I will just let the cool air settle into the edges.

action.why: The card is cool and the floor holds, so I will let the quiet settle.
